Excellent Food and Service
Feb 2020
My wife and I stopped in for dinner recently to try out Maisen Bistro and were delighted by the atmosphere and quality of the food. I had the German sausages with mashed potatoes and sauerkraut while she had the salmon steak. Both were delicious and reasonably priced. There is indoor and outdoor seating available. As mentioned by other reviewers, this restaurant also acts as a school for disadvantaged minority youths from Vietnam, and these young people are learning English as well as important career skills. A wonderful restaurant and a wonderful cause.

Neither good nor really awful.
Dec 2017 • Solo
I chose this restaurant for dinner (19:00). I found it through Tripadvisor.
After reading the few but good reviews I had kind of high expectations and decided to pay them a visit. Besides I already had very good experiences with culinary school restaurants. 
Mai Sen Bistro serves Vietnamese and European food. I mostly went there for the German dishes.
Unfortunately It was a bit of a poor experience. After bringing the menu they did not tell me that they couldn’t serve half of the German main courses since they ran out of pork. The only German dish that appealed to me was “Sauerbraten” (a braised beef dish) which is one of their more expensive dishes at around 200.000 VND. The beef itself was actually good. However the Knödel disappointed a bit and the red cabbage was too cinnamony. 
I expected a generous portion as some people reviewed before. However I was actually still pretty hungry afterwards so I ordered a Bratwurst with fried potatoes and Sauerkraut. That dish neither lived up to the expectations. Sausage was clearly warmed up together with the sauerkraut in the same pan or even microwave container so the whole idea of a bratwurst was none-existent. The fried potatoes were overcooked before frying and was totally bland. The Sauerkraut was actually almost inedible. Since it was ridiculously salty and not really “sauer”
Also that dish was presented as a main but if I wouldn’t have ordered two mains I’d still be hungry. I read that they also bake German style breads for take away and since I’m a German bread enthusiast I wanted to buy a loaf. However they were also out of bread. I would have appreciated a free desert or at least a coffee to compensate for the disappointing experience but that was not the case.

I rated it 3 stars because I do realise it is a school project and I can’t expect everything to be 100% perfect. However I think they learn more from constructive criticism. For that reason I think honesty is the best way to show them where to improve, because I wish they do for their own development. 

Perhaps I will even visit again tomorrow to try the dishes I couldn’t have and see whether I was just unlucky that day.

Dear Tim,
Thank you very much for taking the time to write a review about the Maisen Bistro! 
As you wrote, it is indeed very important for us and our trainees to improve ourselves and to learn for the future.
I am very sorry that you have experienced our service and the food quality as described. 
We ran out of pork and bread on Saturday evening cause the response was larger than we expected, and we ran out before we could serve you. We understand it’s frustrating to miss out on something you looked forward. Additionally I very much apologize the quality of the side dishes on last Saturday evening. We’re working with our kitchen team to ensure that it never happens again. 
We’d hope to welcome you again at our Maisen Bistro!
